Title: Anwar congratulates Zuhairie on Malaysia's first gold at Asian Para Games
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has congratulated national para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi for winning Malaysia's first gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
Anwar said the achievement was even sweeter as Zuhairie had also broken the Games record during the qualifying round.
"Congratulations and well done, Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi. This is a proud start, as you have won the country's first gold medal in the Men's C4-C5 1,000m Time Trial at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.
"Keep pedalling and achieve even greater success. All Malaysians are proud of you," he posted on X.
Zuhairie clinched the gold medal after winning the men's C4-C5 1,000m time trial final at the Izu Velodrome earlier today.
Competing in the C5 category, he clocked one minute 5.361 seconds to secure Malaysia's first gold of the Games.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bursa Malaysia's key index ends below 1,600 support level, baking stocks weigh
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bursa Malaysia's benchmark index extended its decline to close below the 1,600 support level as persistent foreign selling weighed on banking heavyweights, said an analyst.
At 5pm, the FTSE Bursa Malaysia KLCI (FBM KLCI) trimmed 12.01 points, or 0.74 per cent, to 1,595.75 from Friday's close of 1,607.76.
The benchmark index, which opened 3.58 points lower at 1,604.18, moved between 1,593.37 and 1,604.65 throughout the trading session.
On the broader market, decliners outnumbered gainers 741 to 322, while 482 counters were unchanged, 1,299 untraded and 35 suspended.
Turnover fell to RM2.49 billion units worth RM2.38 billion from last Friday's 3.13 billion units worth RM3.27 billion.
For banking counters, Public Bank erased 12 sen to RM4.71, Maybank shed nine sen to RM9.90, CIMB eased five sen to RM7.15, AMMB Holdings slipped 16 sen to RM6.19, and RHB Bank went down 12 sen to RM7.20.
Rakuten Trade Sdn Bhd vice-president of equity research Thong Pak Leng said the equities broker remained cautious, as the sharp sell-off in the domestic market and the FBM KLCI's fall below the 1,600-point level suggested that near-term selling pressure had yet to subside.
Nevertheless, he noted that the correction had brought valuations of selected Malaysian blue-chip stocks to more attractive levels, particularly companies with strong fundamentals, resilient earnings and sustainable dividend yields.
"We believe that this presents opportunities for gradual accumulation once selling pressure begins to ease, rather than signalling a deterioration in the broader domestic economic outlook," he told Bernama.
For the remainder of the week, Rakuten Trade expects the benchmark index to remain volatile, with immediate support at 1,590, followed by 1,580, while a recovery above the 1,600–1,610 range would be necessary to restore market confidence.
"As such, we anticipate the FBM KLCI to trade within the 1,580–1,610 range this week, with selective bargain hunting potentially cushioning further downside," said Thong.
Among other heavyweights, Press Metal jumped 18 sen to RM6.68, YTL Power advanced 11 sen to RM5.26, SD Guthrie improved three sen to RM5.72, while TNB gave up two sen to RM12.98 and IHH Healthcare shaved off 10 sen to RM7.90.
Of the active stocks, Ni Hsin put on 2.5 sen to 44.5 sen, V.S Industry and MAG Holdings were flat at 34 sen and 15.5 sen, respectively, Zetrix AI and JAKS Resources edged down half-a-sen each to five sen and 14 sen, respectively, and Top Glove slid one sen to 89 sen.
Among the top gainers, Nestle garnered 58 sen to RM89.90, Ayer Holdings increased 25 sen to RM7.85, Kuala Lumpur Kepong gained 16 sen to RM20.16, and Petronas Dagangan climbed 14 sen to RM19.78.
The top losers included United Plantations which slid 36 sen to RM30.24, Allianz Malaysia shrank 34 sen to RM19.46, Hong Leong Financial Group erased 28 sen to RM17.56, and Hong Leong Bank was 20 sen easier at RM21.10.

Title: Haze: Johan Setia, Batu Muda among 25 areas with unhealthy air quality
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A total of 25 areas recorded unhealthy air quality as of 5pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor registering the highest Air Pollutant Index (API) reading at 168.
According to the Department of Environment's Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded the second-highest reading at 165, followed by Nilai in Negri Sembilan at 164.
Another 39 locations recorded moderate API readings, including areas in Johor, Pahang, Selangor and Sarawak.
An API reading of 101 to 200 is classified as unhealthy, while readings between 51 and 100 indicate moderate air quality.
Higher API readings indicate greater health risks, particularly for vulnerable groups.
The public, especially children, the elderly and those with respiratory or heart conditions, are advised to limit prolonged outdoor activities when air quality deteriorates.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 buses for MotoGP shuttle service
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL will deploy 85 buses for a special shuttle service to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) during the 2026 Petronas Grand Prix of Malaysia from Oct 30 to Nov 1.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service aimed to meet motorsports fans' transport needs and make their journeys to the circuit more convenient.
He said tickets would go on sale on Oct 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub.
"Every year, motorsports fans from various locations gather in Sepang to experience the excitement of this world-class race firsthand. Rapid KL hopes this service will make their journeys to the circuit easier and more comfortable," he said in a statement today.
Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from 3 locations: the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.
A one-way ticket from Pasar Seni or the KLCC bus stop will cost RM20, while a return ticket will cost RM35. The one-way fare from KLIA Terminal 2 will be RM12.
Buses heading to SIC from all three locations will operate from 7am to 1pm at 30-minute intervals, while return services from the circuit will run from 4pm to 7pm.
In collaboration with SIC, Rapid KL will also provide a free shuttle service around the circuit throughout the event to facilitate visitors' movement.
The public is advised to purchase tickets in advance to avoid long queues and waiting times. Further information is available on the official MyRapid website and through the MyRapid Pulse app.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Khee San in MoU with Paul Lim, sundry goods merchants, to develop digitalization platform for retailers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Khee San Bhd has signed a memorandum of understanding with the Federation of Sundry Goods Merchants Associations of Malaysia and business owner Dr Paul Lim Pang Kiam to develop a digitalisation platform for independent sundry goods retailers.
The platform aims to help retailers adopt digital tools, prepare for e-Invoice requirements and improve operational efficiency and purchasing power.
Under the agreement, Khee San will sponsor and drive the programme, while the association will facilitate member participation, coordinate the selection of pilot retailers and suppliers, and represent members' interests in governance.
"The parties plan to establish a Malaysian private limited company to own and operate the platform, with Khee San as majority shareholder and responsible for day-to-day management," the company said in a Bursa Malaysia filing.
The platform is expected to integrate a retail management system and point-of-sale capabilities, e-Invoice and e-Vendor portals, as well as a group-buying Trading Hub that would pool orders from participating retailers to support bulk purchases and lower procurement costs.
However, the platform's detailed features and commercial arrangements remain subject to further development and definitive agreements.
The parties will also explore government subsidies, determine the pilot cohort and establish a special purpose vehicle, while negotiating definitive agreements covering commercial terms and data governance.
"The indicative roadmap envisages a pilot in months 1 to 6, broader Federation-wide rollout in months 7 to 12, and further scaling from year two, subject to planning and agreement," it said.
Khee San managing director Desmond Yong Loong Chen said the initiative would bring practical digital solutions to independent sundry goods retailers, including tools to improve daily operations and facilitate collective purchasing.
Lim, who originated the programme concept and brought the parties together, said a phased approach would allow the parties to test the model before any wider rollout.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mi Technovation semiconductor material unit launches SGX listing at S$1.80 per share
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Material Holding Ltd, a unit of Mi Technovation Bhd, had launched its initial public offering (IPO) on the Singapore Exchange, pricing its shares at S$1.80 each, to raise a total of S$203.2 million (RM829.58 million).
The listing comprises a total offering of 77.5 million shares. This involves a fresh issuance of 51.5 million new shares by Mi Material, alongside 26 million existing shares offered by Mi Technovation as the vendor.
The issuance is structurally divided into two main tranches; an international offer comprising 71.27 million shares targeted at institutional and selected foreign investors outside the United States, as well as 6.22 million shares to the Singapore public.
Concurrently, a consortium of seven cornerstone investors has executed agreements to subscribe to an aggregate of 41.94 million new shares at the S$1.80 offering price.
The cornerstone backers include abrdn Asia Limited, abrdn Malaysia Sdn Bhd, Amova Asset Management Asia Limited, Areca Capital Sdn Bhd, Barings Singapore Pte Ltd, Fullerton Fund Management Company Ltd, and Manulife Investment Management (Singapore) Pte. Ltd.
Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation Limited and CGS International Securities Singapore Pte Ltd are acting as the Joint Global Coordinators, Bookrunners, and Underwriters for the exercise.
To support price stability upon the commencement of trading, Mi Technovation has granted the underwriters an over-allotment option.
CGS International Securities, acting as the stabilising manager, has the right to purchase up to 5 million additional shares—representing approximately 6.5 per cent of the total offering shares—at the S$1.80 price.
This stabilization window will remain active for 30 days from the listing date on SGX or until the maximum 5 million shares have been bought for stabilising actions.
The execution of this over-allotment option will not increase the total number of issued and outstanding shares immediately following the completion of the offering and cornerstone issuance.
Based on the S$1.80 offer price, the estimated net proceeds from the offering and the issuance of the cornerstone shares, after deducting underwriting fees and estimated offering expenses, will be approximately S$203.2 million.
Approximately S$157.9 million of the proceeds will be due to Mi Material. If the over-allotment option is exercised in full, the estimated net proceeds from the offering due to Mi Technovation will be approximately S$54 million (approximately RM220.45 million).
Mi Technovation will also undertake a dividend-in-specie, to be distributed to its entitled shareholders.
The proposed distribution will involve the distribution of up to 9 million shares to the shareholders of Mi Technovation whose names appear in the record of depositors as of 5.00 pm on Oct 12.
The distribution ratio is one distribution share for every 100 Mi Technovation shares held, excluding treasury shares.
Based on the respective shareholdings of the entitled shareholders as of Oct 12, 8.98 million shares will be distributed to the entitled shareholders.
Mi Material is one of the leading manufacturers of semiconductor advanced packaging materials, engaged in the design, development, manufacturing and commercialisation of precision solder spheres.
Solder spheres serve as critical interconnect components enabling electrical conductivity between integrated circuits and printed circuit boards.
"Our products and solutions are mainly used in end-use applications such as high-performance computing (HPC) for artificial intelligence (AI), memory (including high bandwidth memory (HBM)), mobile devices and wearables, and automotive applications," said the group.
Beyond its core solder spheres, Mi Material also produces solder-related materials and products, including solder ingots, copper core solder spheres, solder paste and solder preforms.
According to Yole, a market research, technology and strategy analysis, Mi Material's market share of the global solder sphere market based on the serviceable addressable market was 24 per cent in 2025.
Mi Materials have been part of Mi Technovation group since April 2021, operating as its semiconductor material business unit. The shareholders of Mi Technovation approved the spin-off of the business unit on Sept 17.
Mi Materials is headquartered in Singapore and currently has production facilities in Tainan, Taiwan and Ningbo, China. It has a combined annual production capacity of our production facilities ranging from approximately 6,600 billion to 8,900 billion solder spheres.
"To support our growth and diversify our production capability, we are in the process of establishing a third production facility in Senai, Johor, which is targeted to be ready for production by the fourth quarter of 2026, with production ramp-up in early 2027, and we plan to expand the production capacity of our facility in Taiwan," said Mi Material.
In addition, the group intends to build a research and development (R&D) and demonstration centre in Texas.
"Over the years, we have established ourselves as a key participant in the global semiconductor advanced packaging supply chain, with long-standing relationships, some of which span over 20 years, with integrated device manufacturers, semiconductor foundries and outsourced semiconductor assembly and test providers across markets including Taiwan, China, Malaysia, the European Union, Singapore, the United States, Japan, Korea and the Philippines," said Mi Material.

Title: Retain SST and improve it instead of reviving GST, says Bangi MP
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should retain the existing Sales and Service Tax (SST) system and improve it where necessary instead of reinstating the Goods and Services Tax (GST), Bangi member of parliament Syahredzan Johan said.
He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim had expressed his willingness during the 2027 Budget engagement session on Aug 18 to incorporate the positive elements of the GST into the existing SST system, including measures to prevent the cascading effect.
"Many parties voiced their support for the GST to be reinstated.
"However, the government should not revert to the GST at this time," he said.
Syahredzan said reintroducing the GST would require more than 900,000 businesses to register and collect the tax, compared with about 132,000 under the current SST system.
"This would certainly mean that the GST would involve far more businesses than the SST," he said when debating the 2027 Budget in the Dewan Rakyat today.
He added that more Sales Tax tariff lines were subject to a zero per cent rate under the SST than under the GST, while more services were taxed under the GST than under the SST.
Syahredzan also said the GST would burden small businesses, which would have to manage tax refunds and other related administrative matters.
Addressing arguments that the GST offered greater transparency, he said the e-invoicing system currently being implemented also aimed to improve transparency.
"However, by exempting micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) with sales below RM3 million from e-invoicing, we have achieved a balance between the need for transparency and avoiding placing a burden on MSMEs," he said.
He said the GST also imposed tax directly on consumers, whereas the tax pass-through mechanism under the current SST system did not impose the tax directly on them.
"Businesses that bear SST on their inputs may indeed be more inclined to prefer the GST, but consumers would bear a heavier impact if the GST were implemented," he said.
Syahredzan said the Madani government had chosen not to reintroduce the GST because it did not want to burden the people.
"We cannot keep changing our tax system every few years. First, we had the SST, then the GST, then the SST again and then the GST once more. We need policy certainty.
"Under the current circumstances, where the people's cost of living is rising, reintroducing the GST would add to the burden on more people.
"As such, the government does not need to revert to the GST. It should continue with the existing system and improve it if necessary," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lorry driver injured after tipper overturns in Shah Alam
Article:
SHAH ALAM: A 40-year-old lorry driver was injured when his 10-tonne tipper lorry carrying rocks skidded and overturned along Jalan Pulau Lumut.
The driver was trapped inside the vehicle.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department assistant director of operations Ashrul Riezal Asbar said firefighters received an emergency call at 3.03pm.
A team of seven firefighters from the Bukit Jelutong Fire and Rescue Station was dispatched to the scene.
"Firefighters extricated the victim, who was pinned inside the vehicle," he said.
Ashrul said the driver sustained minor injuries to his hands and legs. He received medical attention.

Title: Australian lawmaker 'critically' hurt in attack, officials say
Article:
SYDNEY: Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines was deliberately struck by a car and suffered "critical injuries" on Monday in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as an attack.
Haines was hurt outside her office in Wangaratta, just over 200 kilometres northwest of Melbourne, police said.
The 65-year-old "suffered what has been described as critical injuries", Victoria Police Acting Superintendent Ashley Mason said, without identifying the victim in line with police custom in Australia.
The 43-year-old male driver was detained by civilians, Mason said, and then arrested by police, who found a knife in his car.
"This wasn't an accident. There was a deliberate act," Albanese told national broadcaster ABC.
He also told journalists: "All of our thoughts are with Helen, her family, her friends, her team, and her community at this extremely difficult time. We are praying for her full recovery."
The alleged attacker's motive remained unknown, Albanese said, with Australia's counter-terrorism squad activated.
The Australian Federal Police has documented a steady rise in threats and abuse directed towards the nation's politicians in recent years.
They established a dedicated team last year to investigate groups and individuals targeting lawmakers.
Albanese said on Monday that "the temperature has increased in recent times."
"I've expressed that concern to people in the media," he said.
"If you look at anyone's social media feeds and look at the comments, people will say things that they would never say face to face."
Haines entered parliament in 2019 after working as a nurse and midwife, becoming known for stances such as supporting stronger climate action.
She was widely praised for her efforts to increase transparency in politics and crack down on corruption.
"This afternoon, our beloved Helen was involved in an incident outside her Wangaratta Electorate Office, and is receiving medical care," her family said in a statement.
"We thank the swift assistance of bystanders and the dedicated health workers who assisted her, and police for their response."
"Our family, and Helen's staff, will be making no further comment at this time, and ask that their privacy be respected by the public and media," the statement said.
Albanese said Haines was "incredibly hardworking."
"She is fiercely intelligent but, most importantly, she's just a thoroughly decent human being," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 1MDB gets fresh hearing on US$3.78bil judgment against Jho Low, father
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today ordered the High Court to rehear an application by 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) and four of its subsidiaries to set aside a judgment in default (JID) entered against fugitive businessman Low Taek Jho and his father, Tan Sri Larry Low Hock Peng.
A three-judge panel comprising Datuk Azhahari Kamal Ramli, Datuk Ahmad Kamal Md Shahid and Alice Loke Yee Ching allowed 1MDB and its subsidiaries' appeal against a High Court decision that dismissed their application.
Azhahari ordered the case to be remitted to the High Court for a full hearing before a different judge and fixed Oct 26 for case management at the High Court.
Last year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court dismissed the companies' application to set aside the JID on the grounds that they had delayed filing it by nearly three years.
In 2022, 1MDB obtained a JID against Taek Jho, also known as Jho Low, and Hock Peng, ordering them to pay US$3,782,637,525, together with annual interest of five per cent on the respective sums from dates between 2010 and 2014 until full settlement.
The judgment was entered against them after the High Court rejected their defence for failing to comply with a Mareva injunction.
Last year, 1MDB applied to set aside the JID against the two men, seeking to have the dispute proceed to a full trial and to pursue additional relief against them.
The companies claimed that, when the JID was entered, they were unaware of evidence that later emerged in foreign proceedings.
They also said the alleged fraud perpetrated by the defendants was sophisticated and involved multiple entities across various jurisdictions.
A judgment in default is given to a plaintiff when the defendant fails to respond to a summons or appear in court.
1MDB and its four subsidiaries — 1MDB Energy Holdings Ltd, 1MDB Energy Ltd, Global Diversified Investment Co Ltd (formerly known as 1MDB Global Investments Ltd) and 1MDB Energy (Langat) Ltd — filed the US$3.78 billion suit in May 2021 against Jho Low, his father, his mother, Puan Sri Goh Gaik Ewe, his siblings Taek Szen and May Lin, and his associate Tan Kim Loong.
The suit involved allegations of fraudulent concealment, fraudulent misappropriation of funds and unjust enrichment, among other claims.
At today's proceedings, lawyer Lee Shih, assisted by Priyadiana Annadurai, submitted that the companies had been denied a fair hearing because they had not been able to present arguments on the merits of their application to set aside the JID.
Low and his father were neither present nor represented by lawyers in court today.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan schools stay open tomorrow: Outdoor activities halt
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: All educational institutions in Melaka, Selangor and Negri Sembilan, as well as in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong in Pahang, will operate as usual tomorrow, but outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In Melaka, the state education department said students were encouraged to wear face masks, while parents or guardians concerned about their children's health could keep them at home, provided they informed the school.
"School administrators must continuously monitor air pollutant index (API) readings from the Department of Environment (DOE) and pay special attention to students in high-risk groups," it said in a statement.
In Selangor, the state education department said schools would also operate as usual, but outdoor activities had been postponed. Students were encouraged to wear face masks.
The department advised the public to refer to official channels or their respective schools for accurate and up-to-date information. It also reminded school administrators to monitor API readings and pay attention to students in high-risk groups.
In Negri Sembilan, the state education department said all educational institutions under the Education Ministry across the state would operate as usual tomorrow.
"Students are advised to wear face masks, especially those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups," it said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, in Pahang, the state education department, in a Facebook post, said that schools in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong would open tomorrow, but all outdoor and out-of-classroom activities had been postponed.
"Any changes will be communicated from time to time through the respective district education offices," the post said.
In a related development, earlier today, the MOE announced an extension of the deadline for entering marks for several school assessments in the Integrated Education Management System (MOEIS), following disruptions to school sessions and assessment activities due to the haze in several areas.
The deadline for entering marks for the End-of-Academic-Session Assessment (UASA) and End-of-Academic-Session Examinations (PAT/PASA) has been extended by one week, from Nov 21 to Nov 28, while the deadline for entering marks for the Physical, Sports and Co-curricular Assessment (PAJSK) has been extended from Nov 30 to Dec 5.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man remanded four days for threatening, chasing wife with parang
Article:
BATU PAHAT: A smallholder has been remanded for four days after reportedly threatening to chase his wife with a parang over accusations of an affair.
Magistrate Aimi Nawwar Mohamad Othman issued the remand order against the 42-year-old suspect, effective today, to facilitate investigations.
The incident reportedly occurred at a house in Sungai Kalong, Senggarang, at 8.30am yesterday.
Police said initial investigations found that the suspect had taken a 62cm parang and chased his 37-year-old wife while making threats that frightened her.
The incident was witnessed by the woman's mother-in-law and child, following which she lodged a police report.
Police arrested the suspect yesterday to assist in the investigation, which is being conducted under Section 506 of the Penal Code for criminal intimidation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Singapore issues haze notices to three more Indonesian companies
Article:
SINGAPORE: Singapore will issue preventive measure notices (PMNs) to three more Indonesian companies suspected of links to fires in Kalimantan that may have contributed to transboundary haze.
The latest move follows the issuance of similar notices to seven Indonesian companies on Friday over fires in Sumatra, bringing the total targeted under Singapore's Transboundary Haze Pollution Act (THPA) to 10.
The National Environment Agency (NEA) today identified the three additional companies as PT Buana Megatama Jaya, PT Mananjung Hayak, and PT Baratama Putra Perkasa.
"There are indications that smoke from fires in Kalimantan on lands held via concessions under three additional companies in Indonesia could have moved to Singapore," the NEA said.
The seven companies issued notices on Friday were PT Bumi Andalas Permai, PT Bumi Mekar Hijau, PT Paramitra Mulia Langgeng, PT Sumatera Alam Anugerah, PT SBA Wood Industries, PT Hutan Lestari Raya, and PT Bangkanesia.
The NEA said PMNs require companies to deploy firefighting personnel to extinguish blazes on land owned or occupied by them and prevent further spread.
They must also cease or refrain from initiating burning activities and submit action plans detailing measures to extinguish fires and prevent recurrence.
"NEA remains committed to taking enforcement action against errant companies found responsible for causing transboundary haze in Singapore," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: [UPDATED] Teresa Kok wins defamation suit against Akmal, awarded RM250,000
Article:
MELAKA: DAP veteran Teresa Kok has won her defamation suit against Datuk Dr Muhamad Akmal Salleh, with the High Court awarding her RM250,000 in general and aggravated damages.
Kok's lawyer, Datuk Sankara Nair, said in a statement that judge Isa Aziz Ibrahim had also granted an injunction restraining the Umno Youth chief from making further defamatory statements against her.
The court also ordered the removal of the impugned statements from all social media platforms, he said.
In addition, Akmal was also ordered to pay Kok RM50,000 in legal costs.
Sankara said Kok, who is the Seputeh member of Parliament and DAP vice-chairman, welcomed the court's decision.
"She regards the outcome as an important step towards protecting her reputation and holding individuals accountable for defamatory publications.
"Public discourse, including debate on matters of public interest, must be conducted responsibly.
"The freedom to express opinions does not absolve anyone of the legal consequences of publishing defamatory statements about another person," he said.
He said Kok hoped the outcome would serve as a reminder that the right to reputation was protected by law.
"She said social media must not be used as a platform to spread statements that unlawfully damage another person's standing and dignity," he said.
In 2024, Kok filed a
defamation suit against Akmal
over his alleged defamatory remarks about her in relation to the country's halal certification issue.
She claimed Akmal had defamed her in two articles published on a news portal, titled "Akmal: Saya Minta Kerajaan Sediakan Logo Non-Halal, Tampal Pada Dahi Teresa" and "UMNO Youth Chief swipes at 'old Nyonya' Teresa over halal cert".
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Data Centre Bill to be presented to cabinet next year, says Akmal Nasrullah
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: The government plans to draft the Digital Infrastructure (Data Centre) Bill for submission to the cabinet next year to regulate the growth of the data centre industry in line with the country's energy and water supply capacity.
Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir said the measure aims to ensure that investments in the industry add value to the domestic economy while addressing utility constraints and avoiding disproportionate environmental impacts.
He said the proposal was part of the strategic regulatory plan agreed upon by the National Economic Action Council (NEAC) at a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today.
He said the agreement followed a presentation by the Digital Ministry on the National Strategic Direction Towards Sustainable Data Centre Development.
"This step is taken to address utility constraints, avoid disproportionate environmental impacts, and ensure that data centre investments provide real economic spillovers to the local digital ecosystem," he said in a statement.
Akmal Nasrullah said NEAC also agreed that the four lead ministries and the implementing agencies would adopt the Circular Economy Framework (CEF) presented by the Economy Ministry.
"NEAC agreed that the lead ministries, namely the Housing and Local Government Ministry, the Investment, Trade and Industry Ministry, the Science, Technology and Innovation Ministry, and the Human Resources Ministry, along with the implementing agencies, should adopt the CEF with an integrated governance, monitoring and coordination structure," he said.
He said the framework aims to guide the country's transition from a linear economic model based on the "use-and-dispose" concept to a circular economy that optimises the lifespan of materials, reduces waste and preserves resource value.
"This integrated policy was formulated to address fragmented implementation across ministries in the past, prevent economic losses caused by the loss of valuable resources, and support the Net Zero aspiration by 2050," he said.
In other developments, Akmal said the meeting also reviewed the National Economic Resilience Framework presented by the Economic Affairs Division of the Prime Minister's Office as a comprehensive long-term measure to address external economic shocks.
"The meeting agreed that this proposal should be presented to the Cabinet and discussed further at a meeting of ministry secretaries-general and heads of service chaired by the Chief Secretary to the Government," he said.
He said NEAC had examined three strategic policy priorities to drive sustainable growth and strengthen the country's economic resilience amid structural challenges and global economic uncertainties.
He said the agreed policies must be implemented in an integrated manner, particularly to improve resource-use efficiency, ensure data centre investments add value to the domestic economy, and strengthen the country's preparedness for external economic shocks.
Akmal said the Economy Ministry, as NEAC's secretariat, would coordinate and monitor follow-up actions with the relevant ministries and implementing agencies.
"The government's priority is not just growth and investment, but a more productive, sustainable and resilient economy that delivers real benefits to the people and businesses," he added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three houses damaged after trees fall in Bayan Lepas
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: Three houses were damaged after three trees fell on their roofs at Kampung Bukit, Bayan Lepas, today.
No casualties were reported.
Penang Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director John Sagun Francis said the department received an emergency call at 12.56pm.
He said firefighters found the trees on the roofs of the 3 houses when they arrived at the scene.
"We found the three trees on the roofs of three houses, partially damaging the structures.
"No injuries were reported," he said in a statement.
Firefighters cut up and cleared the fallen trees with assistance from other agencies at the scene.
The operation involved four personnel from the Seri Balik Pulau fire and rescue station, supported by the civil defence force, police, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Gertak Sanggul volunteer fire brigade.
The situation was brought under control at 2.42pm, and the operation concluded at 2.46pm after firefighters ensured there were no further hazards.
John said the site was subsequently handed over to MBPP for further action.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Police record statements from 15 in RM230.9mil MyEG, Zetrix AI probe
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have recorded statements from 15 people to assist investigations into the alleged failure to remit RM230.9 million in government revenue collections involving electronic service providers MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd.
Federal Commercial Crime Investigation Department director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said in a statement that those questioned comprised 12 Road Transport Department (RTD) officers and three bank officers.
He said the case is being investigated under Section 409 of the Penal Code for criminal breach of trust.
"The investigation concerns the suspected failure to transfer government revenue collections amounting to RM230,913,503.55 involving the two companies," he said.
On Oct 13, Rusdi
confirmed that police
had recorded six statements following a police report lodged on Oct 7 to assist investigations.
It was reported that RTD had suspended the services of MyEG Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MYEG Group, as its collection agents effective Oct 5.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the decision followed a review of the companies' compliance with the terms and conditions of their agreement, as well as outstanding obligations that remained unresolved.
The suspension came after the Transport Ministry separately confirmed to business news portal The Edge that Zetrix AI owed the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections.
The amount involved money collected from customers for vehicle road tax and driving licence renewals, as well as traffic summonses.
Zetrix AI, formerly known as MYEG Services Bhd, has provided online government services, including those linked to RTD, since 2000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bangi MP calls for fair allocations regardless of political affiliation
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government should enact legislation to guarantee constituency allocations for all members of parliament (MPs), regardless of political affiliation, Bangi MP Syahredzan Johan said.
He said the amount allocated should be determined using a proportional formula to ensure fair distribution.
The lack of legislation or guidelines guaranteeing allocations to all MPs, regardless of political affiliation, was an issue that needed to be addressed in 2027 Budget, he said.
"This is in line with the concept of a national covenant, which emphasises the government's trust and responsibility to act fairly and do its best for the people after receiving their mandate," he said.
Syahredzan was speaking during the debate on the Supply Bill (2027 Budget) in the Dewan Rakyat.
DAP national chairman Gobind Singh Deo had also called on the government to enact legislation guaranteeing fair allocations to all MPs without political discrimination.
Gobind, who is also Damansara MP, said the law could remove political discretion in the allocation of funds, ensure transparency and protect the rights of voters nationwide.
He said the proposal was in line with Pakatan Harapan's election pledge to ensure fair development allocations for all MPs.
Syahredzan, who is also DAP national deputy chairman, said allocations should not be equal in amount because constituencies differed in size and voter numbers.
He cited Bangi, which has more than 300,000 voters and about 700,000 residents, compared with other constituencies with only half or a third as many voters.
He said giving Bangi the same allocation as other constituencies would also be unfair because, based on a rough calculation, its voters would receive a lower allocation than those in other areas.
He asked the government to
enact legislation guaranteeing allocations
to all MPs, with the amounts determined using a proportional formula to ensure fairness.
Syahredzan also called on the government not to reintroduce the Goods and Services Tax (GST), saying more than 900,000 businesses would need to register and collect the tax.
This was far higher than the about 132,000 businesses currently registered under the Sales and Services Tax (SST), he said.
He said GST would burden small businesses with the administration of tax refund claims and directly tax consumers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Record El Nino? Depends who's counting
Article:
BRITAIN'S Met Office says this year's El Nino is "unprecedented." Japan's weather agency has called it the strongest ever observed. US forecasters say it still trails the biggest events in its record books.
How can they all be right?
The answer lies in how they measure El Nino's strength, with meteorological agencies using different methods to assess the climate phenomenon that make direct comparisons difficult.
"By any measure, we are looking at a very strong El Nino," climate scientist Emily Becker of the University of Miami told AFP, adding that only once it is over will scientists be able to assess how big it is and "where it fits in the context of history."
The Pacific Ocean's El Nino Southern Oscillation (ENSO) is the planet's main natural climate driver.
Normally, trade winds blow east to west along the equator, pushing warm water from South America toward Asia, while cold water rises from the depths to replace it.
El Ninos, which occur every two to seven years on average and last nine to 12 months, disrupt this pattern.
The trade winds weaken and warm water is pushed back east toward the Americas. That shift in where ocean heat is released into the atmosphere ripples across global weather, making some regions cooler and wetter and others hotter and drier.
In describing the El Nino as unprecedented, the Met Office points to raw temperatures in the Pacific.
"Our observations confirm that sea-surface temperatures in the central equatorial Pacific have now surpassed levels recorded during previous El Nino events," it said in a statement to AFP.
But absolute temperatures are just one way of measuring El Nino's strength. Agencies also look at anomalies – how far temperatures rise above a historic baseline – to assess the event.
The Japan Meteorological Agency last week declared this El Nino the strongest on record based on how far sea surface temperatures were above normal in the Nino3 region of the eastern Pacific.
By its count, the event beat 1997 in observations going back to 1949.
The US watches a neighbouring box, Nino3.4, in the east-central Pacific.
It declares an El Nino when temperatures there run at least 0.5C above normal and the atmosphere responds, weakening the trade winds and shifting tropical rainfall eastward.
[[nid:1559045]]
This process is known as "ocean-atmosphere coupling."
How "normal" is defined has been a matter of significant debate.
The US National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) and other agencies including the UN's World Meteorological Organisation long used the Oceanic Nino Index (ONI), which compares temperatures to a 30-year average that is updated every five years, so that the baseline keeps pace with a warming climate.
But with climate change speeding up and warming oceans worldwide, NOAA now uses the Relative Oceanic Nino Index (RONI), and the WMO is in the process of switching.
RONI also relies on a 30-year average but goes on to measure how warm or cool the east-central Pacific is compared to the rest of the tropical ocean, because it is that difference that drives the weather impacts we care about.
"We were finding a mismatch between the temperature of the tropical Pacific and the impacts," said Becker about the old index.
La Nina years, when the central and eastern tropical Pacific is cooler than normal, were producing stronger effects than their rating suggested, and El Ninos weaker ones.
NOAA projects this El Nino will be the strongest in its records, which go back to 1950, if the three-month average RONI anomaly reaches 2.5C or higher, a level that would put it above the 1982-83, 2015-16, and 1997-98 events.
The chances are rated "high," but not yet certain.
"Regardless of where we're ranking or how we're measuring this event, it's an incredible opportunity to study and understand this very powerful phenomenon in the context of a warming world," said Becker.
* The writer is from AFP
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Speaker tells MPs to exercise caution when using religious terms
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Members of Parliament have been reminded to exercise caution when using religious terms that could lead to misunderstandings and prolonged disputes in the Dewan Rakyat.
Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul said words such as "munafik" (hypocrite) might be familiar to those with a deep understanding of religion but not to those less familiar with their meaning, including non-Muslims.
"I did not attend a religious school. I went to an English school, and I am extremely wary of using words with profound meanings that I may not understand.
"If someone accused me of being a munafik, I would immediately fall ill because I did not come from a religious school," he said in the Dewan Rakyat.
He said the same applied to Muslims and non-Muslims who might feel apprehensive upon hearing such terms, particularly when they were used by individuals with religious knowledge.
Johari said MPs should be mindful of the differing levels of understanding among their fellow MPs when using religious terminology.
He suggested that MPs opt for less controversial language to prevent debates from dragging on unnecessarily.
"We do not need to show that we are knowledgeable or that we attended religious schools. Such language can create an intimidating situation when others do not understand it."
He said disputes over the use of such terms wasted parliamentary time that should instead be spent addressing issues affecting the people.
Earlier, proceedings in the Dewan Rakyat turned tense following a war of words between government and opposition MPs over the use of "munafik" in reference to Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
The exchange erupted after RSN Rayer (PH-Jelutong) invoked Standing Order 36(1), objecting to the use of the term by Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN-Kota Baru) during the debate on the 2027 Supply Bill.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Three women arrested over fake medical certificates in Kota Tinggi
Article:
KOTA TINGGI: Three women were arrested here yesterday afternoon to assist in investigations involving fake medical certificates (MCs) used to deceive employers in the district.
District Police Chief Superintendent Yusof Othman said the three women, aged between 22 and 23, were detained at 3.20pm.
He said the arrests followed a police report lodged by a medical officer from a private clinic regarding fake MCs at 2.47pm on Oct 5.
"Initial investigations revealed the first suspect is believed to have purchased a fake medical certificate before submitting the document to her employer.
"The second suspect acted as a middleman to help obtain the fake medical certificate from the third suspect," he said in a statement today.
Yusof said checks showed that one of the three suspects has a prior record for a narcotics offence.
"Police believe the arrests will assist investigations into several cases involving forged medical leave documents around the Kota Tinggi district.
"The case is being investigated under Section 420 of the Penal Code for cheating and Section 471 of the Penal Code for using as genuine a forged document. The suspects have been remanded until Thursday to facilitate investigations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RM500 monthly aid to support Norhazwani's two daughters
Article:
TUMPAT: The sister of Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) officer Norhazwani Ibrahim, who was killed last week, is expected to receive RM500 in monthly assistance to help care for the victim's two young daughters.
Kelantan Social Welfare Department director Che Samsuzuki Che Noh said the aid would be provided under the Foster Child Assistance scheme, which allocates RM250 per child each month.
However, he said the assistance could only be disbursed to Marliza Ibrahim, 48, after the court officially granted custody of the children to the victim's family.
"We will expedite the process once the court has decided on the custody arrangements," he told reporters after visiting Norhazwani's family in Kampung Telaga Lanas.
Che Samsuzuki said an initial assessment by the department's counsellors from Tumpat and the Kelantan headquarters found that the victim's two daughters, aged five and six, could be placed under Marliza's care.
He said Marliza had agreed to look after the children, and the victim's family had also supported the arrangement.
"We will closely monitor the children's welfare and assess whether the family needs further assistance.
"We will also provide immediate aid through the department's emergency assistance fund, along with essential supplies and items needed by the children," he said.
Meanwhile, Norhazwani's elder brother, Amran, thanked the department for its assistance.
"We will use the money for my two nieces' future. Both of them will be enrolled in preschool in Pengkalan Kubor," he said.
Norhazwani was allegedly murdered by her husband at their home in the KLIA quarters in Nilai, Negri Sembilan, last Thursday.
She was reportedly stabbed twice in the left abdomen and once in the right cheek.
The suspect
surrendered to police
shortly after the incident and was remanded for seven days to assist investigations under Section 302 of the Penal Code for murder.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Australian teens disclose online sexual harm to AI chatbots
Article:
CANBERRA: Australian teenagers who experience online sexual abuse are more likely to disclose it to artificial intelligence (AI) chatbots than to authorities, a national study has found, reported Xinhua.
The study of almost 2,000 Australians aged 16 to 18, conducted in early 2026 by Adelaide University's Australian Cybercrime Observatory, found that 18.7 per cent of victims told an AI about their experience.
Meanwhile, 13.2 per cent reported it to a teacher, doctor, counsellor, police officer or helpline, according to a university statement released on Monday.
More than one in four cases of nonconsensual sharing of sexual images involved AI, while at least one in 25 Australians had experienced, or had a close friend who had experienced, AI-related online sexual victimisation before the age of 18, showed the findings published in Child Abuse & Neglect.
Girls experienced higher rates of online sexual victimisation overall, but boys were significantly more likely to be targeted when AI was involved, it said.
More than one-third of adolescents also expressed concern that AI could be used to create fake images of themselves or people they cared about.
The findings highlighted the need for reporting pathways accessible through AI tools, peer-focused prevention and broader efforts to protect children, researchers said.
"AI involvement in this abuse is worryingly common, and victims are now more likely to tell an AI than teachers, doctors, police or reporting services.
"We must adapt quickly to protect children," said Associate Professor Timothy Cubitt from Adelaide University, who is also the study's co-author.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Two men fined RM6,000 each for stealing telecommunications components
Article:
GUA MUSANG: Two men were each fined RM6,000 by the magistrate's court here today after pleading guilty to stealing telecommunications components at the Chiku 3 Felda transmission tower site earlier this month.
Mohd Syahrul Mohamed Sarip, 40, and Mohd Fahmi Mat, 31, entered their pleas after the charges were read out before magistrate Nik Mohd Tarmizie Nik Mohd Shukri.
They were jointly charged with stealing telecommunications components at the Chiku 3 Felda transmission tower site about 3pm on Oct 2.
The offence is punishable under Section 379 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of up to seven years, a fine or both.
Deputy public prosecutor Siti Asma'a Che Omar prosecuted, while the two men were represented by lawyer Ahmad Firdaus Abdul Hamid from National Legal Aid Foundation.
Nik Mohd Tarmizie fined both men RM6,000 each.
Meanwhile, Syahrul was also charged with stealing five remote radio units belonging to CelcomDigi Bhd at the PBTS Blue Valley Lojing transmission tower about 6pm on Oct 3.
The offence is also punishable under Section 379 of the Penal Code.
For this charge, Nik Mohd Tarmizie fined Syahrul RM7,000. Both men paid their respective fines.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Bus Cap appoints Ma Xiyin as independent, non-executive director
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Bus Cap Bhd, Malaysia's first pure-play bus builder listed on Bursa Malaysia, has appointed Ma Xiyin as an independent non-executive director, effective Oct 16.
The appointment strengthens the board's expertise in new-energy technologies and electric mobility as the group expands beyond conventional bus manufacturing, the group said in a statement.
"We welcome Ma Xiyin to the Board of Bus Cap. Her experience across China's new-energy and electric mobility industries brings valuable perspectives at an important stage of our group's development," said Bus Cap executive director Bernard Ng Chong Yan.
Ma has more than 15 years of experience in business leadership, strategic investments and commercial development within China's new-energy and electric mobility sector.
She is currently managing director of the Aiduke business group, which has interests in electric vehicles, electric buses, charging infrastructure, battery and energy storage systems, renewable energy projects and new-energy components.
Ng said the transportation industry's next phase of growth would extend beyond vehicle manufacturing, with charging infrastructure, energy storage, technology and lifecycle services becoming increasingly important.
"Ma's commercial exposure to these areas is particularly relevant as we evaluate new opportunities in the new-energy commercial vehicle market," he said.
He added that Ma's experience would complement the existing board as the group evaluates international partnerships, technology localisation and potential business expansion.
The appointment follows Bus Cap's memorandum of understanding with BYD Malaysia Sdn Bhd on Aug 18 to explore a strategic cooperation framework for a Malaysia-based new-energy commercial vehicle platform.
The proposed collaboration includes establishing an electric bus assembly and manufacturing facility in Perak, alongside product localisation, sales, marketing, distribution and after-sales services.
Ng said the collaboration marked an important step in the group's transition towards a broader mobility platform.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Housewife loses nearly RM88,000 in fake online investment scam
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU: A 63-year-old housewife lost RM87,975.04 after being duped by a non-existent online investment scheme.
Kuala Terengganu police chief Assistant Commissioner Azli Mohd Noor said the victim came across a stock investment advertisement on Facebook on Oct 3.
He said the woman was attracted to the scheme and contacted a male suspect via WhatsApp to inquire further.
"The suspect persuaded the victim to join the scheme by promising lucrative returns of RM25,000 for every RM450 invested.
"Lured by the prospect of high returns, the victim made nine transactions totalling RM87,975.04 using her savings and money obtained by pawning her jewellery between Oct 3 and Oct 12," he said in a statement today.
Azli said the victim realised she had been cheated after failing to recover her initial capital or receive the promised profits, while attempts to contact the suspect were unsuccessful.
"The victim, who is from Wakaf Tembusu in Kuala Nerus, lodged a police report at 7.58pm yesterday," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: BKE traffic diversion near Lunas on Oct 21 for emergency drill
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Traffic on the Butterworth-Kulim Expressway (BKE) heading east towards Lunas, Kedah, from Butterworth-Kubang Semang will be diverted via the Penanti eastbound rest and recreation (R&R) area on Wednesday.
Plus Malaysia Berhad (Plus) said in a statement today that the diversion would be in effect from 10.30am to 12.30pm to facilitate an emergency simulation exercise.
"The exercise will test the efficiency, response times, preparedness and actions of PLUS, rescue teams and relevant agencies when dealing with highway emergencies.
"It will also assess and review the efficiency of rescue procedures for accident victims by the relevant rescue agencies," it said.
The exercise will involve Plus personnel and various agencies, including the Malaysian Highway Authority, police and fire and rescue department.
Other participants include the Health Ministry, Department of Environment, Civil Defence Force, Prifaria Sdn Bhd, a strategic transport partner, and highway maintenance contractor Edgenta Infrastructure Services.
Motorists can obtain the latest traffic updates via the Plus app, its virtual assistant Putri, Plus social media platforms, including its X account @plustrafik, and electronic message signs (VMS) near the exercise site.
They can also contact Plusline at 1800-88-0000 for assistance during emergencies.
PLUS thanked highway users for their patience and cooperation during the exercise.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Calls grow to bring Malaysian elephants home
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Three Malaysian elephants at Tennoji Zoo in Osaka, Japan, are reportedly showing signs of severe emotional distress, prompting calls for their immediate return, an activist group said.
The three elephants, named Dara, Amoi and Kelat, were transferred to the zoo in March.
Pertubuhan Konservasi Alam Malaysia activist Dr Siti Rabiah Raws said the elephants had been observed displaying repetitive stereotypical behaviour, including excessive head swaying.
"This behaviour is a clear sign of severe psychological distress and possible zoochosis," she said when contacted yesterday.
Oxford University elephant expert Dr William Keith Lindsay has backed calls for the elephants' return, having prepared three reports urging their immediate repatriation to Malaysia.
Siti Rabiah said Kelat's frequent musth cycles required urgent attention. She said Dr Lindsay had pointed out that male elephants typically undergo musth only once or twice a year.
Musth is a periodic biological condition in adult male elephants marked by a surge in testosterone, heightened aggression and intense reproductive behaviour.
"This, combined with Kelat's prolonged separation from Dara and Amoi, raises serious questions about the animal's welfare and the suitability of the facility.
"We believe Kelat must undergo an independent veterinary assessment and be closely monitored," she said.
Siti Rabiah said the organisation had sent two staff members to Tennoji Zoo in April to record the elephants' daily behaviour.
Taiping Municipal Council president Tuan Mohamed Akmal Dahalan declined to comment when contacted.
"I cannot respond personally. When the time comes, I will issue an official statement on the latest developments," he said.
In August, the council said Kelat, Dara and Amoi were healthy and active, and that Tennoji Zoo's keepers and veterinary officers monitored their condition regularly.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: China set to leave benchmark lending rates unchanged for 17th month
Article:
SHANGHAI: China is set to leave benchmark lending rates unchanged for a 17th consecutive month in October, a Reuters survey showed, after better-than-expected third-quarter GDP data lessened prospects for near-term easing.
The loan prime ‌rate (LPR), normally charged to banks' most creditworthy clients, is calculated each month after 20 designated commercial banks submit proposed rates to the People's Bank of China (PBOC).
In a Reuters survey of 22 market ⁠participants conducted this week, all respondents predicted that the one-year ​and five-year LPRs would remain unchanged at three per cent and 3.50 per cent, respectively, ​at the upcoming review on Tuesday.
China's economic growth bounced off three-year lows in the third quarter, as roaring exports offset consumers' tight grip on their wallets, though analysts warn the growing reliance on external drivers is deepening structural imbalances.
Market participants expect Beijing to reach its 2026 growth target of 4.5 per cent to five per cent without resorting to additional stimulus, helped by a strong start to the year and some recent modest fiscal and monetary support.
The overwhelming consensus for steady LPR settings comes as some major economies tilt towards tighter monetary policy to contain ​inflation pressures, while China's long-dated bond yields hovered near a 15-month low.
Investors are turning to a key financial forum in Beijing this afternoon, where PBOC Governor Pan Gongsheng is due to speak, for clues on the country's monetary path.
Meanwhile, China's new home prices fell again in September, extending a more than three-year slump and suggesting policy support has yet to spark a broad-based recovery in housing demand.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Sarawak set to become Borneo's international arbitration hub
Article:
KUCHING: Sarawak is set to become a regional hub for international arbitration in Borneo with the establishment of an office of the Asian International Arbitration Centre (AIAC) in the state, said Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
She said the office was also expected to spur international business and trade activities in Borneo.
"The facility will provide opportunities for legal practitioners in Sarawak and Sabah to explore international arbitration, which operates according to international standards, particularly as Sarawak is experiencing rapid growth in business and international trade.
"The establishment of the second office after Kuala Lumpur is expected to expand AIAC's activities in Sarawak while benefiting the legal community, particularly lawyers in Sarawak and Sabah," Azalina told reporters after attending the signing ceremony for the agreement to establish the AIAC Sarawak office, witnessed by Sarawak Premier Tan Sri Abang Johari Tun Openg.
The agreement was signed by Sarawak State Secretary Datuk Amar Mohamad Abu Bakar Marzuki and AIAC chief executive officer Datuk Danesh Chandran.
Azalina said the Sarawak government had not only approved the proposal but also allocated RM10 million to upgrade the Kuching Textile Museum building, which will house the AIAC Sarawak office.
She said the establishment of AIAC Sarawak also reflected Malaysia's efforts to strengthen its position as a destination for international-standard dispute resolution services.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rapid KL to deploy 85 shuttle buses for Malaysian GP at Sepang
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct19 — Rapid KL will deploy 85 buses for a special shuttle service to the Sepang International Circuit (SIC) in conjunction with the 2026 Petronas Grand Prix (GP) of Malaysia from October 30 to November 1.
Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Syahrul Azmir Ahmad Zaki said the service was aimed at meeting the transport needs of motorsports fans and facilitating their journeys to the circuit.
He said tickets would go on sale from October 22 at selected customer service counters and the Pasar Seni Bus Hub.
“Every year, motorsports fans from various locations gather in Sepang to experience the excitement of this world-class race firsthand. Rapid KL hopes this service will make their journeys to the circuit easier and more comfortable,” he said in a statement today.
Syahrul Azmir said the shuttle service would operate from three main locations, namely the Pasar Seni Bus Hub, the KLCC bus stop and the KLIA Terminal 2 Bus Hub.
A one-way ticket from Pasar Seni or the KLCC bus stop will cost RM20, while a return ticket will be priced at RM35. The one-way fare from KLIA Terminal 2 is RM12.
Buses travelling to SIC from all three locations will operate from 7 am to 1 pm at 30-minute intervals, while return services from the circuit will run from 4 pm to 7 pm.
In collaboration with SIC, Rapid KL will also provide a free shuttle service around the circuit throughout the event to facilitate visitors’ movement.
The public is advised to purchase tickets in advance to avoid long queues and waiting times. Further information is available on the official MyRapid website and through the MyRapid PULSE app. — Bernama

Title: Anwar congratulates para cyclist Zuhairie on winning Malaysia’s first gold at 2026 Asian Para Games
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim congratulated national para track cyclist Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi for winning Malaysia’s first gold medal at the 2026 Asian Para Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan.
Anwar said Zuhairie’s achievement was made even sweeter by the fact that the athlete also broke the Games record during the qualifying round.
“Congratulations and well done, Zuhairie Ahmad Tarmizi. This is a proud start, as you have won the country’s first gold medal in the Men’s C4-C5 1,000m Time Trial at the 2026 Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games.
“Keep pedalling and achieve even greater success. All Malaysians are proud of you,” he posted on X today.
Zuhairie secured Malaysia’s first gold medal at the Games after winning the men’s C4-C5 (physical impairment) 1,000-metre (m) time trial final at the Izu Velodrome earlier today.
Zuhairie, competing in the C5 category, clocked a time of one minute 5.361 seconds for Malaysia’s first gold medal of the Games. — Bernama

Title: Haze: 27 areas in Malaysia record unhealthy air quality as of 4pm, Johan Setia in Selangor records highest reading of 169
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — A total of 27 areas nationwide continued to record unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 4 pm today, with Johan Setia in Selangor recording the highest reading of 169.
According to the Department of Environment’s (DOE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS) portal, other areas in Selangor, including Petaling Jaya (158), Klang (156), Banting (154) and Shah Alam (153), also recorded unhealthy readings.
Three areas in Melaka were also at the unhealthy level, namely Alor Gajah (165), Bukit Rambai (164) and Bandaraya Melaka (161), as were Nilai (164), Seremban (164) and Port Dickson (120) in Negeri Sembilan.
Meanwhile, in Kuala Lumpur, Batu Muda and Cheras recorded readings of 164 and 152, respectively, while Putrajaya recorded 154.
Six areas in Johor also recorded unhealthy API readings, namely Tangkak (161), Pasir Gudang (157), Batu Pahat (156), Larkin (140), Kota Tinggi (128) and Kluang (105).
Other affected areas were Rompin (155) and Indera Mahkota Kuantan (152) in Pahang; IPD Serian (139) and Sri Aman (113) in Sarawak; and Tasek Ipoh (136), Pegoh Ipoh (125) and Seri Manjung (114) in Perak.
A total of 38 areas nationwide recorded moderate API readings, while only three areas - Labuan (48), Kimanis in Sabah (43) and Limbang in Sarawak (35) - recorded good readings.
An API reading of zero to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy, while readings above 300 are hazardous. — Bernama

Title: Haze: Schools in Melaka, Selangor, Negri Sembilan and Pahang to open tomorrow, outdoor activities suspended
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — All educational institutions in Melaka, Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, as well as in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong in Pahang, will operate as usual tomorrow, but all outdoor activities have been suspended due to the haze.
In Melaka, the State Education Department said that students attending school were encouraged to wear face masks, while parents or guardians who were concerned about their children’s health were allowed to keep them at home, provided that they informed the school.
“School administrators must continuously monitor the Air Pollutant Index (API) readings from the Department of Environment (DOE), and pay special attention to students at high risk,” it said in a statement.
In Selangor, the State Education Department also said that schools would operate as usual, but outdoor activities had been postponed, with students attending school encouraged to wear face masks.
The department also advised the public to refer to official channels or the schools for accurate and up-to-date information, while reminding school administrators to monitor API readings and pay attention to high-risk students.
In Negeri Sembilan, the State Education Department said that all educational institutions under the Ministry of Education (MOE) across the state would also operate as usual tomorrow.
“Students are advised to wear face masks, especially those experiencing respiratory symptoms or belonging to high-risk groups,” it said in a statement today.
Meanwhile, in Pahang, the State Education Department, in a Facebook post, said that schools in Kuantan, Rompin and Bentong would open tomorrow, but all outdoor and out-of-classroom activities had been postponed.
“Any changes will be communicated from time to time through the respective district education offices,” the post said.
In a related development, earlier today, the MOE announced an extension of the deadline for entering marks for several school assessments in the Integrated Education Management System (MOEIS), following disruptions to school sessions and assessment activities due to the haze in several areas.
The deadline for entering marks for the End-of-Academic-Session Assessment (UASA) and End-of-Academic-Session Examinations (PAT/PASA) has been extended by one week, from November 21 to November 28, while the deadline for entering marks for the Physical, Sports and Co-curricular Assessment (PAJSK) has been extended from November 30 to December 5. — Bernama

Title: MyEG probe into RM230.9m govt revenue case widens, 15 questioned, including 12 JPJ officers
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The police have recorded statements from 15 individuals to assist in investigations into allegations of failure to transfer RM230.9 million in government revenue, involving MyEG Sdn Bhd (MyEG) and Zetrix AI Berhad.
Bukit Aman Commercial Crime Investigation Department (CCID) director Datuk Rusdi Mohd Isa said those questioned comprised 12 Road Transport Department (JPJ) officers and three bank officers.
“So far, statements have been recorded from 15 individuals, comprising 12 from JPJ and three bank officers,” he said today.
He said that the investigation was launched following a police report, received on Oct 7, concerning financial transactions involving government revenue linked to the two companies under the MyEG Group.
The case is being investigated under Section 409 of the Penal Code.
On October 13, Rusdi was reported to have said that police had recorded statements from six witnesses, while various related documents were being examined to assist in the investigation.
He had also reminded the public against speculating about the case, and stressed that legal action would be taken against any parties found to be involved. — Bernama

Title: Businessman loses appeal to claim RM185,671 lottery prize without ticket in Shah Alam court
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — A businessman has failed in his bid to recover RM185,671 from Pan Malaysian Pools Sdn Bhd after losing his winning lottery ticket.
At the Shah Alam High Court today, judicial commissioner Seow Hock Peng dismissed M Mahendravarman’s appeal against a Sessions Court ruling that rejected his claim against the lottery operator,
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT) reported.
The court also ordered him to pay RM3,000 in costs.
Mahendravarman said he purchased a ticket bearing the numbers 1515 and 1010 for RM30 at a Petaling Jaya outlet on May 14, 2022, and won RM185,671 in the draw. He photographed the ticket but later misplaced it.
He lodged a police report on May 16, 2022 and attempted to claim the prize using the photograph.
The company refused to pay without the original ticket.
According to FMT, during the appeal, counsel R Kengadharan argued that the sessions court had placed undue weight on the missing ticket while overlooking supporting evidence.
He pointed out that the company’s witness confirmed the serial number in the police report matched the photograph of the ticket, and that no one else had produced the original to claim the prize.
Kengadharan cited provisions of the Evidence Act 1950 to support the admission of secondary evidence in cases where original documents are lost.
The company’s lawyer, Shamala Devi Balasundaram, countered that its rules required the original ticket to prevent fraud or duplicate claims.
Kengadharan said he would seek instructions from his client on whether to pursue a further appeal.

Title: Lawyer says eviction bid halted, court order to be sought for Balai Undang Rembau
Article:
REMBAU, Oct 19 — The Balai Undang Luak Rembau today faced another attempt at eviction when several senior government officials arrived to reclaim possession of the premises.
The effort was not carried through after discussions between the parties concluded with agreement that any eviction must follow proper legal process and be backed by a clear court order, as reported by
Kosmo! Online
.
Lawyer representing the Balai Undang Luak Rembau, Emirul Sarifudin Nor Azmi, said those present included the director of the Land and Mines Office (PTG), the Rembau district officer, the district police chief and several other department heads.
“On this day, we were informed that the other side came to enter and take back possession of the Balai Undang Luak Rembau. “However, after discussions, all parties agreed that any action must be based on the law and respect the institution of the monarchy,” he told
Kosmo! Online
here today.
Emirul Sarifudin said following the talks, the authorities would file a fresh application in court under the name of the PTG director to obtain a vacant possession order for the building.
“After the agreement was reached, all parties dispersed without any eviction being carried out,” he was quoted as saying.

Title: Poultry farm operator slapped with RM50,000 fine for fly breeding offence
Article:
PARIT BUNTAR, Oct 19 — A poultry farm operator was fined RM50,000 by the Magistrate’s Court here today after pleading guilty to two charges of allowing fly breeding at two poultry farm premises in Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, last July.
Magistrate Salwa Asmary Abdul Rahim imposed a fine of RM25,000 for each charge against Datuk Siah Gim Eng, 67, and ordered the issuance of a warrant to levy distress on the company’s property under Section 283(1)(iii) of the Criminal Procedure Code if he failed to pay the fines.
Siah, who was unrepresented, paid the fines.
According to the first charge, Siah was accused of allowing fly breeding at a PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm at Lot 5020, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 9.40 am on July 16.
He was also charged with committing the same offence at another PWF Farms Sdn Bhd poultry farm along Jalan Changkat Lobak, Beriah, Gunung Semanggol, Kerian, at 12.16 pm on the same day.
Both charges were framed under Section 17(1) of the Poultry Farming (Amendment) Enactment 2023 (Enactment A51) and are punishable under Section 17(2) of the same enactment, which provides for a maximum fine of RM50,000, imprisonment for up to three years, or both.
According to the facts of the case, a team of officers from the Perak Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) inspected both broiler chicken farms and found fly infestations exceeding the department’s prescribed threshold.
The farm at Lot 5020 housed 88,000 broiler chickens in 14 open-sided coops and recorded a fly infestation level of 27.6, above the department’s maximum threshold of 14.
The second farm in Beriah housed 190,000 broiler chickens in 14 open-sided coops and recorded a fly infestation level of 23.2.
Larval samples collected from both premises were sent to the Parasitology and Haematology Laboratory at the Veterinary Research Institute (VRI) in Ipoh, where they were identified as belonging to the Muscidae family, which includes houseflies and stable flies.
Further investigations revealed that the farms had previously been issued compounds twice each in 2025 for similar offences, amounting to a total of RM30,000.
In mitigation, Siah appealed for a lower fine, citing his responsibility for the welfare of his employees.
However, DVS Perak prosecuting officer Roziman Awang Tahrin urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, taking into account the previous offences, to deter similar violations, prevent recurrence and safeguard public health and environmental hygiene in the local community. — Bernama

Title: Religious scholars must keep up with advances in science and technology, says Zulkifli
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Religious scholars need to broaden their knowledge by keeping abreast of developments in science, technology and geopolitics to ensure that the message of
dakwah
remains relevant in addressing contemporary global challenges.
Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Religious Affairs) Dr Zulkifli Hasan said mastery of contemporary knowledge must go hand in hand with the study of traditional Islamic knowledge and ‘turath’ (Islamic classical heritage) to enable religious scholars to understand global changes and address the challenges facing the ummah more comprehensively.
He said developments in areas such as post-quantum cryptography, quantum computing and superintelligence warranted attention because of their implications for cybersecurity, the economy and geopolitical competition.
“Quantum computing technology has the potential to break the security systems currently used in banking, communications, government and personal data,” he said in a Facebook post.
He also referred to developments in the United States, which has been paying attention to super intelligence technology, including an executive order titled ‘Inaugurating the Era of Super Intelligence’, signed by President Donald Trump on Sept 29.
Zulkifli said global technological and geopolitical developments required society, including religious scholars, to understand strategic issues and avoid becoming preoccupied with trivial matters and differences of opinion that offered little benefit.
He said post-quantum cryptography was also important in efforts to protect data from future threats posed by quantum computers, particularly in security systems used in the banking, communications and government sectors.
Meanwhile, he expressed gratitude that Malaysia had emerged as the only Asean country to achieve the highest level, Tier 1, in post-quantum cryptography migration readiness.
Zulkifli said an understanding of global issues and strategic thinking was important to ensure that religious scholars provided guidance with wisdom and firmness, and were able to address the challenges facing the ummah comprehensively.
“Science and technology must be mastered as tools to safeguard religious integrity, grounded in the values of ‘syarak’ (Islamic law),” he said.
In another development, Zulkifli stressed the importance of preserving bonds of friendship and brotherhood through dakwah and local arts and culture, referring to the recent reunion of members of rock band XPDC at a concert.
He said differences of opinion within society or organisations were normal and should not affect fraternal ties.
“The reunion is a beautiful manifestation of how differences of opinion are normal and should not tear apart the bonds of friendship and brotherhood among people,” he said.
He said artistic works could also serve as a medium to nurture the public’s soul and convey spiritual messages and lessons in life.
“Through songs such as
Sedekah
and
Titian Perjalanan
, as well as their anthem,
Kita Peng Yu
, they have demonstrated that art can educate the soul and encourage society to return to the values of goodness,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Traffic diversion on Butterworth-Kulim Expressway for two hours from 10.30am on Oct 21
Article:
BUTTERWORTH, Oct 19 —Highway users on the Butterworth-Kulim Expressway (BKE) between KM16.7 and KM17.7 will be diverted for two hours on October 21 for an emergency simulation exercise.
PLUS Malaysia Berhad said in a statement that the diversion would be in effect from 10.30 am to 12.30 pm, affecting westbound traffic travelling from Butterworth/Kubang Semang towards Lunas.
During the exercise, affected motorists will be diverted through the eastbound Penanti Rest and Service Area (R&R).
The exercise aims to assess PLUS and the relevant agencies’ preparedness, response time and coordination in handling highway emergencies, as well as evaluate accident response and safety procedures.
Participating agencies include PLUS, the Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM), Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM), Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM), Health Ministry (KKM), Department of Environment (DOE), Malaysia Civil Defence Force (APM), transport strategic partner Prifaria Sdn Bhd and highway maintenance contractor Edgenta Infrastructure Services (EIS).
