Motorists can obtain the latest traffic updates through the PLUS app, PUTRI Virtual Assistant, PLUS social media platforms, including its @plustrafik account on X, and variable message signs (VMS) near the exercise area.
For emergency assistance, the public can contact PLUSLine at 1800-88-0000. — Bernama

Title: KL JPJ records RM376,091 in proceeds from seized vehicle auction
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Kuala Lumpur Road Transport Department (JPJ) generated RM376,091 from its Public Auction of Seized Vehicles (Series 2/2026), conducted through the JPJvBID system.
Its director, Hamidi Adam, said 120 of the 157 vehicles offered were successfully auctioned, surpassing the results of the previous auction series.
In addition to the proceeds from vehicle bids, RM34,650 was generated from the sale of 693 e-catalogues, while auction fees amounted to RM7,400 from 740 payment transactions recorded throughout the auction period.
“The highest bid was RM73,333 for a Toyota Alphard, while the lowest was RM101 for a Yamaha Lagenda that could not be licensed for road use as it was classified as a scrap vehicle,” he said in a statement today.
Hamidi said the results reflected the effectiveness of the JPJvBID system as a transparent, efficient and accessible digital auction platform.
He added that Kuala Lumpur JPJ remained committed to enhancing efficient, transparent and customer-oriented service delivery in line with the public service’s digital transformation agenda. — Bernama

Title: Wan Saiful urges Putrajaya to consider shutting pig farms, says imported pork ‘safer’, may be cheaper
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — Opposition lawmaker Wan Saiful Wan Jan today urged the federal government to consider shutting down pig farms nationwide, as Putrajaya reviews the industry chain.
According to
Malaysiakini
, the Wawasan Negara vice president said any approach must avoid racial or religious sensitivities and instead focus on practical concerns such as pollution, public welfare and sustainability.
“Personally, I feel it would not be excessive for me to propose that the federal government consider whether it is appropriate for Malaysia to continue having large pig farms when pork supplies can be obtained through imports, as done in Singapore.
“In fact, imported pork may be cheaper than that farmed in Malaysia,” he was quoted as saying in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Wan Saiful added that pig farming in Malaysia was likely to face opposition from local residents regardless of location, describing Singapore’s reliance on imports as a “safer” approach.
His remarks echoed a proposal made in January by Kalam Salan (PN Sabak Bernam), who similarly called for pig farming operations to cease and for pork to be imported to meet local demand.
Agriculture and Food Security Minister Mohamad Sabu had in March announced a comprehensive study of the sector, covering legal, technical, economic and social aspects.
The minister also disclosed that 121 of the 355 registered pig farms nationwide have already adopted modern systems, including closed house and zero discharge models.

Title: Court of Appeal revives 1MDB bid to challenge US$3.7b judgment against Jho Low and father
Article:
PETALING JAYA, Oct 19 — The Court of Appeal today gave 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB) and four of its subsidiaries another chance to challenge a High Court ruling that ordered fugitive financier Low Taek Jho, better known as Jho Low, and his father, Larry Low Hock Peng, to pay more than US$3.7 billion.
According to
Free Malaysia Today
(FMT), the three member bench, chaired by Justice Azhahari Kamal Ramli, directed that the application be heard afresh before a different High Court judge. Case management has been fixed for October 26.
Justice Azhahari, sitting with Justices Ahmad Kamal Shahid and Alice Loke, made no order as to costs.
The appeal stemmed from the Kuala Lumpur High Court’s refusal last year to set aside a judgment in default obtained by the five companies in 2022.
That judgment was entered after the defendants’ defences were struck out for breaching a Mareva injunction, which prohibits parties from dissipating assets.
The five companies had asked for the judgment to be set aside so the case could proceed to a full trial and allow them to seek wider remedies against Jho Low and his father.
However, the High Court dismissed the application on the ground that it was filed out of time.
Lawyer Lee Shih, assisted by Priyadana Annadurai, appeared for 1MDB and its subsidiaries. Neither Jho Low nor his father was present or represented in court.

Title: PAC launches probe into Sabah Pan Borneo Highway after audit reveals delays despite RM10.5b spent
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — The Public Accounts Committee (PAC) has launched an investigation into the management, financial governance and physical implementation of Phase 1 of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project following revelations in the Auditor-General’s Report (LKAN) Series 2/2026.
PAC chairman Datuk Mas Ermieyati Samsudin said that from 2016 to March 31, 2026, RM10.547 billion, or 94.6 per cent of the RM11.153 billion allocation, had been spent, although the project’s physical progress was far behind schedule.
She disclosed that the 706-kilometre (km) project, comprising 35 work packages, was expected to be fully completed by the end of 2021, but only four work packages, or 11.4 per cent, had been completed.
“While the remaining 31 work packages, worth RM16.319 billion, are still being implemented, the project should have been completed five years ago.
“Of these, nine work packages are classified as sick projects, while 13 are behind schedule. Only nine work packages are ahead of schedule,” she told a press conference at the Parliament building today.
Mas Ermieyati said that, due to weaknesses in planning, the project’s completion date had been extended to 2030, while the overall contract cost had increased from RM17.910 billion to RM18.394 billion.
She said the Auditor-General’s Report also revealed that 57 Variation Orders amounting to RM513.99 million had been approved beyond the authorised limits without the approval of the Secretary-General of the Treasury or the Works Ministry’s Procurement Board.
In addition, the projected current cost for the 15 Phase 1A work packages had surged by RM987 million to RM11.323 billion, compared with the original ceiling cost of RM10.336 billion, while interim payments totalling RM163.64 million had been made to contractors and consultants without formal contractual agreements.
“Government advance funds amounting to RM41.37 million for utility works have yet to be recovered from utility companies, despite the six-month deadline following the issuance of the Certificate of Partial Completion (CPC) having passed,” she said.
The audit report also revealed that 19 work packages had commenced before the Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) report was approved, while 77,299 monitoring data files had been lost due to the ineffective use of the Project Information System.
However, Mas Ermieyati said the PAC took note of a statement by Sabah Deputy Chief Minister I and Works and Utilities Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam, who said that the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway Phase 1 packages were being actively constructed.
“The unfinished Sabah Pan Borneo Highway Phase 1 packages are now being actively constructed, with some sections recording physical progress of between 90 and 93 per cent. Eight packages covering 179km have been proposed to be opened in stages before the end of this year,” she said.
She said the investigation was also initiated following an official request from the Kota Belud Member of Parliament (MP) and concerns raised by the Sipitang, Beaufort and Balik Pulau MPs during the debate on the Auditor-General’s Report in the Dewan Rakyat on October 7.
Mas Ermieyati said the PAC would summon witnesses from the Works Ministry, the Public Works Department (JKR), including JKR Sabah, and relevant agencies for the investigation proceedings.
“If the PAC proceedings uncover any indications of misconduct, corruption or abuse of power, the committee will not hesitate to refer its findings to the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) and the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for further investigation,” she said. — Bernama

Title: On loan to Japan, welfare row over Dara, Amoi and Kelat flares up again as Taiping council holds off on latest claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — An activist has renewed calls to bring home three Malaysian elephants from a Japanese zoo, claiming they are showing signs of serious emotional distress.
Dara, Amoi and Kelat have lived at Tennoji Zoo in Osaka since March under a 25-year cooperation deal with Taiping Zoo & Night Safari.
Siti Rabiah Raws of the Environmental Conservation Association of Malaysia said all three have been seen shaking or swinging their heads excessively and repeatedly, which she called “a clear sign of extremely severe emotional distress and possibly the mental disorder zoochosis”.
She said such behaviour calls for a professional assessment of the elephants’ psychological health,
Berita Harian
reported today.
Her group has had two staff at Tennoji Zoo since April, recording the elephants’ behaviour daily.
Siti Rabiah also raised concerns over Kelat, who is reported to have gone into musth six to seven times in the seven months since he arrived.
Musth is when a mature male elephant’s hormones go into overdrive, which can make him moody, aggressive and hard to handle.
Siti Rabiah said Oxford University elephant expert William Keith Lindsay told her bull elephants typically experience musth once or twice a year, making the reported frequency worth scientific scrutiny.
Lindsay, who also backs bringing the elephants home, is reported to have prepared three comprehensive reports urging their immediate return to Malaysia.
Siti Rabiah said Kelat’s long separation from Dara and Amoi adds to the worry, and she called for an independent veterinary assessment and close monitoring of him.
Taiping Municipal Council president Mohamed Akmal Dahalan declined to comment on the allegations when contacted,
Berita Harian
reported.
He said he could not respond personally and that the council would issue an official statement on the elephants’ latest condition when the time comes.
The Taiping council has previously rejected claims of neglect, saying in May that Kelat’s behavioural changes were linked to the natural musth phase and that all three elephants had gained weight.
In June, it said Kelat had been housed separately during musth for safety reasons and had since been reintroduced to Dara and Amoi.
In August, the council said the three elephants were healthy and active, and that Tennoji Zoo’s keepers and veterinarians were monitoring them regularly.
The elephants’ welfare has been a public issue since earlier this year, with Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Datuk Seri Arthur Joseph Kurup saying proposals to repatriate them deserve serious consideration.
His deputy, Syed Ibrahim Syed Noh, has said the process cannot be rushed, while the Taiping council has said repatriation would require clear evidence of a breach of the agreement’s welfare terms.

Title: Papagomo walks free after acquittal on sedition charge over Facebook remarks
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — Blogger Wan Muhammad Azri Wan Deris, better known as Papagomo, was acquitted and discharged by the Klang Sessions Court today of a sedition charge over remarks allegedly made on Facebook three years ago.
His lawyer, Muhammad Rafique Rashid Ali, said Judge Siti Aminah Ghazali delivered the decision at the conclusion of the defence case.
“The court noted that the defence had successfully raised a reasonable doubt, while the prosecution had failed to prove its case beyond a reasonable doubt,” he told Bernama when contacted today.
He said only Wan Muhammad Azri, 43, testified for the defence, while Deputy Public Prosecutor Mohamad Mustaffa P. Kunyalam prosecuted the case.
On July 31 this year, the Kuala Lumpur High Court ordered Wan Muhammad Azri to enter his defence after allowing the prosecution’s appeal against an earlier Sessions Court decision acquitting him.
On September 3 last year, Siti Aminah acquitted and discharged the blogger, ruling that the prosecution had failed to establish a
prima facie
case against him. However, the High Court subsequently overturned that decision and ordered him to enter his defence.
On January 8, 2024, Wan Muhammad Azri pleaded not guilty to a charge of making seditious remarks on Facebook by allegedly claiming that the government was pro-Israel and pro-Western.
He was accused of making the remarks on the Facebook page of Halid Hamidi, also known as Halid Mat Kool, which an individual at a condominium unit in Jalan Tong Shin, Bukit Bintang, here, viewed at 1 pm on Nov 8, 2023.
The charge was framed under Section 4(1)(b) of the Sedition Act 1948, which provides for a maximum jail term of three years, a fine of RM5,000, or both, upon conviction. — Bernama

Title: Finance Ministry staff urged to use ‘ATM’ approach to fast-track Budget 2027
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Finance Ministry (MoF) staff have been urged to adopt the principles of ‘Amanah, Tangkas dan Mudah Cara’ (ATM) or Trust, Agility and Facilitation, to strengthen governance and accelerate the implementation of government policies and programmes under Budget 2027.
Treasury Secretary-General Tan Sri Johan Mahmood Merican said the principles also underscored the need for MoF to set an example for other ministries and agencies in implementing governance reforms, while ensuring that every government allocation was used effectively for the benefit of the people.
Speaking at the Finance Ministry’s monthly assembly today, he said trust must form the foundation of the ministry’s workforce, particularly in ensuring transparency and integrity in public financial management.
The event was officiated by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim, who is also Finance Minister. Also present were Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan, Deputy Finance Minister Liew Chin Tong, Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar and Public Service Department director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz.
Johan said the reforms to be implemented included the enforcement of the Government Procurement Act next year and the disclosure of details of all government contracts, including those awarded through direct negotiations, except those involving security matters.
He said MoF would also draft a State-Owned Enterprises Act to strengthen governance in the investment and procurement activities of government-owned entities, including statutory bodies and companies under Minister of Finance Incorporated (MOF Inc).
“On governance, the Prime Minister also announced that MoF would draft a State-Owned Enterprises Act to strengthen governance, particularly in investment and procurement by government-owned entities, including statutory bodies and MOF Inc companies.
“The Prime Minister intends to prevent abuses similar to those that occurred at 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB), Tabung Haji and the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) from recurring in the future,” he said.
On agility, Johan said ministry staff had been reminded to improve efficiency and speed in decision-making and facilitate the implementation of government projects, in view of the public’s increasingly high expectations.
He said the Chief Secretary to the Government had directed all ministries and officers to begin planning and procurement processes earlier to ensure that projects directly benefiting the people could be implemented promptly, as government projects typically only began to show progress in the second quarter of the year.
“MoF will also explore allowing procurement processes to begin without having to wait for the issuance of allocation warrants,” he said.
On facilitation, Johan said the principle required MoF staff not to focus solely on procedural compliance but also to seek solutions to help other ministries and agencies implement programmes that benefited the country.
However, he said such efforts must remain within the scope of existing powers and regulations, while ensuring that every project delivered the best value for money and did not cause losses to the government.
Johan also urged MoF staff to make efforts to assist the people, particularly vulnerable groups, a key performance indicator (KPI) for next year.
“I encourage everyone to adopt the KPI of doing good and helping someone through the authority we have.
“I hope this can be practised alongside efforts to help the Prime Minister realise the MADANI Economy agenda, implement and expedite programmes under Budget 2027, and support the government’s overall agenda for next year and beyond,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Deputy minister: No payment delays affecting Pan Borneo Highway project
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — There have been no delays in payments to contractors working on the Pan Borneo Highway project that could affect construction progress, Deputy Works Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Maslan told the Dewan Rakyat today.
He said payments for Phases 1A and 1B were being made in line with physical progress, with disbursements keeping pace with or exceeding scheduled levels.
“Phase 1A, comprising 15 work packages, had achieved 89.54 per cent physical completion against a scheduled 96.23 per cent, while financial disbursements stood at 88.78 per cent.
“For Phase 1B, which has only recently begun, actual physical progress stands at 25.53 per cent, ahead of the scheduled 24.76 per cent.
“Financial disbursements have reached 22.11 per cent, exceeding the scheduled 20.73 per cent. Therefore, there is no issue with payments,” he said in reply to Datuk Wetrom Bahanda (KDM-Kota Marudu) on whether delays in the project were caused by late payments to contractors or the appointment of contractors lacking the necessary expertise.
Ahmad also acknowledged that contractor performance remained a concern that needed to be addressed to keep the project on track.
He said the Works Ministry had tightened monitoring through monthly meetings to review construction progress and resolve emerging issues.
The meetings, chaired by the Sabah State Secretary and the ministry’s Secretary-General, were part of efforts to ensure the project was implemented effectively, he said.
The ministry has also introduced measures to prevent further delays, including strengthening steering committees and special task forces to assess contractor performance, identify causes of delays and develop solutions.
These measures are aimed at ensuring the Pan Borneo Highway project is completed on schedule, he added. — Bernama

Title: Malaysia advocating Asean self-reliance in essential medicines, says Dzulkefly
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Malaysia is spearheading efforts to strengthen Asean’s self-reliance in essential medicines and reduce dependence on vulnerable global supply chains as part of a broader push to enhance regional health security, said Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad.
He said Malaysia is taking a leading role in advancing the Asean Drug Security and Self-Reliance (ADSSR) initiative, recognising the urgent need to build stronger regional capacity to safeguard access to critical medicines.
“Health security demands stronger regional capacity to secure essential medicines, rather than reliance on fragile external supply chains,” he said when delivering Malaysia’s country statement at the 77th Regional Committee Meeting for the Western Pacific in Manila, the Philippines, here today.
Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s commitment to strengthening regional health security is reflected in its leadership of the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting and the ADSSR initiative.
He said Malaysia is also pursuing structural reforms aimed at building a more sustainable healthcare system with greater emphasis on disease prevention, early detection and digital health transformation.
“We are bringing non-communicable disease (NCD) screening closer to communities, using fiscal measures such as sugar taxation, applying behavioural insights to encourage healthier choices, and strengthening our digital health architecture for early detection,” he said.
Dzulkefly said Malaysia’s Lung Health Initiative is another key component of the country’s healthcare reforms, integrating screening and treatment into primary healthcare settings.
He said the initiative aims to ensure continuity of care, from screening and early diagnosis to treatment and follow-up for both communicable and NCD lung diseases.
He said the government is adopting a whole-of-society approach by bringing together healthcare providers, civil society organisations, and the private sector to address common health risks, improve public awareness and reach the underserved populations.
On global health governance, Dzulkefly reaffirmed Malaysia’s support for reforms to the international health architecture amid financial volatility and geopolitical tensions.
He said Malaysia, through its participation in a task force alongside Japan and under China’s co-chairmanship, is advocating greater inclusivity for developing countries and Small Island Developing States.
He also stressed that the World Health Organisation (WHO) must translate policy recommendations into concrete action through partnerships that deliver measurable benefits to communities.
“WHO’s leadership, particularly the director-general (DG) and our regional director leadership, must move from advice to action, driving partnerships that deliver tangible results on the ground,” he also said.
Dzulkefly added that Malaysia envisions a resilient Western Pacific region where health supplies are secure and preventive healthcare is embedded at every level, while remaining ready to share its experience and translate regional solidarity into decisive, practical action.
Dzulkefly is currently leading the Malaysian delegation to the 77th Regional Committee Meeting for the Western Pacific from Oct 19 to 22 and is scheduled to pay a courtesy call on WHO DG Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus and deliver an intervention statement on the WHO Programme Budget under Agenda Item 8.
Tomorrow, Dzulkefly will participate in a ministerial roundtable discussion on the Regional Health Essential Stockpile and Pooled Procurement Mechanism under Agenda Item 13 and pay a courtesy call on WHO regional director for the Western Pacific Dr Saia Ma’u Piukala.
He is also expected to hold bilateral meetings with two candidates for the WHO DG post, namely Dr Hanan Mohamed Al Kuwari of Qatar and Budi Gunadi Sadikin (Indonesia). — Bernama

Title: Ten‑minute war of words in Dewan Rakyat over Takiyuddin’s ‘munafik’ remark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Proceedings in the Dewan Rakyat turned heated today after a war of words broke out between government and opposition MPs over the use of the term “munafik”, allegedly directed at Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim.
According to
Berita Harian
(BH), the exchange, which lasted nearly 10 minutes, began when RSN Rayer (PH–Jelutong) raised Standing Order 36(1), claiming that Datuk Seri Takiyuddin Hassan (PN–Kota Bharu) had used the word while debating the Supply Bill 2027.
He argued that the term was offensive and inappropriate, particularly when aimed at the prime minister.
Rayer questioned why Deputy Speaker Alice Lau Kiong Yieng had allowed Takiyuddin to continue without intervening.
“It is an offence for MPs to use offensive language. I heard him cite a verse from the Quran, followed by the word ‘munafik’ directed at the prime minister, and we just let it pass?” he was quoted as saying.
Takiyuddin, who is Perikatan Nasional’s chief whip, was reported to have earlier cited a hadith describing the traits of a munafik (hypocrite), before referring to the word waad (promise) used by Anwar in his Budget 2027 speech.
Rayer repeatedly attempted to interject to raise a point of order but was ignored until Lau eventually halted Takiyuddin’s speech, BH reported.
The incident then drew the attention of Datuk Awang Hashim (PN–Pendang), who insisted that Rayer had misunderstood Takiyuddin’s remarks.
Lau later advised Rayer to submit a formal motion to the Speaker’s office for further action, saying: “I have already given guidance — file a motion and send it to the Speaker’s office. That is all.”

Title: Roland Sagah says 680 Sarawak schools unsafe, calls for urgent upgrades
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 19 — A total of 680 schools in Sarawak have been classified as unsafe for occupancy, highlighting the scale of infrastructure upgrading needed across the state, said Datuk Seri Roland Sagah Wee Inn.
The Education, Innovation and Talent Development Minister said the schools were categorised under Scale 6 and 7, indicating the need for substantial investment in upgrading and improvement works.
“Under the RM1 billion advance payment allocation, 86 dilapidated school projects have been completed, while the remaining 54 are at various stages of implementation,” he said during his ministerial winding-up speech at the State Legislative Assembly (DUN) sitting.
Meanwhile, under ‘Projek Rakyat’, Sagah noted that six of the 12 identified projects had been completed, while the remaining six were either under implementation or at the pre-construction stage.
Sagah also expressed appreciation to the federal government for allocating RM1.3 billion under Budget 2027 to upgrade 682 dilapidated schools nationwide, particularly in Sabah and Sarawak.
“It is hoped that a substantial portion of this allocation will be channelled towards upgrading school infrastructure and improving facilities in Sarawak,” he added. — The Borneo Post

Title: Which book says 1MDB debts are all paid? Anwar wants to know
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today dismissed claims that all 1Malaysia Development Bhd (1MDB) debts have been paid.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said the government is still footing the bill, interest included,
The New Straits Times
reported.
“Some say all 1MDB debts have been paid. I don’t know what book they read that from, but it is not true.
“Our debts, including the interest, must be paid,” he was quoted as saying at the Finance Ministry’s monthly assembly here.
The Finance Ministry has put the government’s total 1MDB-related obligations at RM51.4 billion, of which RM42.5 billion has been paid and RM8.9 billion remains outstanding.
It has also said RM31.3 billion has been recovered through asset recovery efforts, which would leave a net burden of RM20.1 billion if no more money is clawed back.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, said repayments on old debts must carry on even as the government keeps a tight lid on new borrowing and works to reduce the national debt.
He said a responsible government borrows only what it must to manage the economy, while planning ahead.
“You should not burden the future generation to pay for the excesses of the present,” he was quoted as saying.
Anwar said sound fiscal management must go hand in hand with strong governance and political will.
He cited the Public Finance and Fiscal Responsibility Act as one way of strengthening parliamentary oversight.
The Parliamentary Services Act, he said, shows the government’s commitment to curbing executive powers and boosting democratic accountability.

Title: Sarawak infectious disease centre 90pc complete, set for launch in 2027
Article:
KUCHING, Oct 19 —The Sarawak Infectious Disease Centre (SIDC) is 90 per cent complete as of August 2026 and is expected to be officially launched in the third quarter of 2027.
Sarawak Minister for Education, Innovation and Talent Development Datuk Seri Roland Sagah Wee Inn said the RM320 million facility would support disease surveillance and research into infectious diseases.
He said SIDC’s Disease Surveillance Programme (DSP) had conducted 13 exercises across southern Sarawak, involving more than 1,000 participants.
The exercise in Gedong Pangkor also marked the launch of SIDC’s first mobile laboratory.
“In 2027, the programme will expand to eight sites in central Sarawak, including Kapit, Sebauh and Mukah, to strengthen disease surveillance and public health interventions,” he said when winding up the debate on his ministry at the Sarawak State Legislative Assembly here today.
Sagah said SIDC had also initiated a pharmacogenomic pilot study using PacBio human genome sequencing to identify genetic variants associated with adverse reactions to tuberculosis treatment.
The study aims to support more personalised antibiotic treatment based on individuals’ genetic profiles.
Meanwhile, Sagah said Sarawak would host the World Robot Olympiad (WRO) Open Championship in 2027.
He described the event as a significant milestone for Sarawak and a testament to the continued growth of its science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and robotics ecosystem.
“Hosting the WRO Open Championship in 2027 will provide a valuable opportunity to showcase Sarawak’s homegrown talent on the international stage while welcoming students, educators, coaches and robotics enthusiasts from around the world,” he added. — Bernama

Title: Penang secures RM33.22b for 280 federal development projects
Article:
GEORGE TOWN, Oct 19 — A total of 280 federal development projects in Penang, with a combined cost of RM33.22 billion, have been approved under the Second Rolling Plan (RP2) of the 13th Malaysia Plan (13MP) for 2027.
In a statement today, Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the projects comprise 44 new projects and 236 ongoing projects, with RM2.68 billion allocated for implementation in 2027.
The 44 new projects have a combined cost of RM578.29 million, with RM63.71 million allocated for next year, he said.
Of these, four state priority projects submitted by the Penang state government in February have also been approved, Chow said.
The four projects are the Sungai Keluang Ubi Flood Mitigation Scheme in Central Seberang Perai; the upgrading of Jalan Bukit Tambun FT149 from the Jalan Persekutuan FT001 junction to the Bukit Tambun Selatan Toll junction in Simpang Ampat, South Seberang Perai; the Sungai Perai Flood Mitigation Scheme (Phase 2) in Central Seberang Perai; and the mapping and development of the state’s groundwater resources.
Chow said the four projects have a combined cost of RM96.95 million, with RM2.2 million allocated for 2027.
Another state priority project, the Penang STEM Talent Blueprint, had been approved earlier under the First Rolling Plan (RP1) of the 13MP, at a cost of RM12.3 million, he added.
“The state government will continue to strengthen strategic cooperation with the federal government to ensure development allocations are optimally utilised to advance the state and improve the people’s well-being.
“This includes joint efforts to establish the Penang Technology Financial Centre, envisioned as the country’s technology-focused financial hub. The centre is expected to contribute RM12.1 billion to gross domestic product and support more than 71,000 jobs over the next 15 years,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Selangor Palace seeks investigation into alleged fake Raja Muda bodyguard
Article:
SHAH ALAM, Oct 19 — The Selangor Palace has expressed serious concern over allegations that an individual had impersonated the Raja Muda of Selangor’s personal bodyguard to deceive members of the public for financial gain.
In a statement, the Office of the Sultan of Selangor said it had received reports concerning the alleged impersonation, which involved purported deals for land and luxury cars.
“The Selangor Palace administration takes this matter seriously and has referred it to the Royal Malaysia Police for a thorough, fair and transparent investigation.
“The palace will not protect anyone found to be involved in the case,” it said.
The palace also urged the public to verify with its administration any claims by individuals purporting to represent or have connections with the royal household before entering into transactions.
It stressed the importance of checking the authenticity of such claims to avoid falling victim to fraudulent dealings.
Meanwhile, Selangor police chief Datuk Shazeli Kahar confirmed that a police report was lodged on October 15 by the Sultan of Selangor’s Security Control Office at Istana Mestika over the alleged impersonation.
“The report concerns the misuse of the Raja Muda of Selangor’s photograph by the owner of a Threads account, ‘dwan_hamid’, who allegedly posed as the Raja Muda’s aide-de-camp (ADC) to deceive members of the public in property and vehicle transactions.
“An investigation paper has been opened under Section 420 of the Penal Code, and efforts are under way to trace the suspect,” he said in a statement today.
Shazeli also advised the public to remain vigilant and verify claims through official channels before making financial transactions to avoid falling victim to scams. — Bernama

Title: Zahid tells Negri Sembilan representatives to put public welfare first
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Barisan Nasional (BN) chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi has advised the coalition’s 18 Negeri Sembilan state assemblymen to stay out of matters involving customary law and the royal institution, and instead focus on the people’s welfare and fulfilling their mandate.
The Deputy Prime Minister said matters concerning customary law and royal institutions should be kept separate from the administration of the state government to ensure that public services were not disrupted.
“My advice to our BN assemblymen is not to interfere any further in matters involving the Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang and the royal institutions. We should focus on delivering services because the people elected their representatives and gave them a mandate,” he said.
He was speaking to reporters after launching the Road Safety Congress 2026 at the Malaysia International Trade and Exhibition Centre (MITEC) here today.
Also present were Transport Minister Anthony Loke Siew Fook, Deputy Transport Minister Datuk Hasbi Habibollah and Malaysian Institute of Road Safety Research (MIROS) chairman Prof Dr Wong Shaw Voon.
Ahmad Zahid said the Negeri Sembilan government was preparing a draft of the state’s 2027 Budget despite not having a full state executive council (Exco) line-up at present.
He said priority must be given to engaging with the people and addressing their problems, regardless of any issues that might arise.
“What is important is that, whatever problems arise, priority must be given to engaging with the people and addressing their concerns,” he said.
He expressed hope that cooperation between the state government and the 11 assemblymen who were not aligned with it could continue to ensure that the state administration was not left in limbo and that the government machinery could function as usual.
On political cooperation for the upcoming Melaka state election, Ahmad Zahid said he had reviewed the matter and had asked Melaka Chief Minister Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh to announce a decision soon. — Bernama

Title: Dr Mahathir thanks Malaysians for support after Hasmah’s passing, says strength has yet to fully return
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 19 — Former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad today thanked Malaysians for their support, prayers and assistance following the death and burial of his wife, Tun Dr Hasmah Mohamad Ali, while acknowledging that he has yet to fully regain his strength.
In a Facebook post today, Dr Mahathir said he had attempted to return to his office over the past few days but remained physically weak.
“Over the last day or two, I tried going to the office but my strength has not yet fully returned,” he said.
Speaking on behalf of his family, the 101-year-old statesman expressed his gratitude to all those who helped facilitate Hasmah’s funeral arrangements.
He also said he was deeply touched by the continual prayers offered for his late wife, whether at her gravesite or from elsewhere.
Dr Mahathir said the outpouring of support reminded him to remain grateful to Allah despite the pain of his loss, saying he had been blessed to share so many years of his life with Hasmah.
“In the midst of such painful sadness, it reminds me to continue being grateful to Allah for having entrusted Hasmah to me for such a long time, until this stage of my life,” he wrote.
He also apologised to those whose greetings, waves or condolences he had not been able to acknowledge during the period of mourning.
“I would also like to take this opportunity to apologise if there were greetings I did not respond to, waves I did not return, and messages of condolence that I have yet to answer. Thank you,” he said.
Hasmah, his wife of more than seven decades, passed away on September 28, 2026.

Title: PM Anwar says subsidy rationalisation toughest act, but vital to curb wastage
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Oct 19 — Subsidy rationalisation is one of the toughest economic acts but it is necessary to plug wastages and leakages in Malaysia, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
Anwar, who is also the Finance Minister, said even his predecessors such as Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad and Datuk Seri Najib Razak had attempted the measure but lacked the determination to implement it.
“Not many countries have managed to make it (subsidy rationalisation) work and few countries dare to even attempt doing it,” Anwar said during the Finance Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
“The economic theories may not support it but for leaders committed to the Waad Nasional, we are obliged to do our best for the people,” he added.
Anwar said his administration has also increased cash aid allocations under Sumbangan Tunai Rahmah (STR) and Sumbangan Asas Rahmah (SARA) to RM15 billion, up from the RM8 billion earmarked by the previous administration.
“We actually estimate the cash aid allocations to increase up to RM18 billion,” he said.
Anwar also urged civil servants in the Finance Ministry and related agencies to improve their competency and reduce bureaucratic delays, especially as they now enjoy higher wages and better living conditions.
“No great empires in history have suffered decline because they have helped to uplift the people. But, many declined because of greed, rampant corruption and abuse of power,” he added.

Title: DKU hauls Negeri Sembilan MB Ismail Lasim, 16 others to court over throne dispute
Article:
SEREMBAN, Oct 19 — The Negeri Sembilan Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) and its secretary Raja Norazli Raja Nordin have gone to court seeking permission to start contempt proceedings against Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, 10 former state executive councillors and six others.
The application, filed at the Seremban High Court on Oct 15, names 17 individuals. They include the menteri besar, the former exco members whose appointments were revoked in September, and six plaintiffs in an ongoing case.
The DKU says the group ignored a court order issued on June 5, which barred them from interfering in the council’s affairs or changing its status quo. That order is still in force.
Despite that, the six plaintiffs are alleged to have continued backing a disputed proclamation over the Negeri Sembilan throne, making public statements and holding press conferences between September and October to declare it valid.
The menteri besar and the exco members are accused of pushing ahead with the proclamation by endorsing it at a state executive council meeting on September 15, sending a letter to the Keeper of the Rulers’ Seal on September 17, and suspending senior state officials on September 22.
The case is now pending before the High Court.

Title: ECRL fares start at RM60 for Gombak-Kuantan route, RM125 one-way to Kota Bharu
Article:
GOMBAK, Oct 19 — Fares for the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) will start from as low as RM60 one way for Economy Transit services between Gombak and Kota Sultan Ahmad Shah (KotaSAS) in Kuantan, Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) said today.
Economy Transit tickets for the 523km Gombak-Kota Bharu route will start at RM125 one way, while Express fares will start at RM147.
MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak said the Cabinet approved the fares on October 16 under an “affordable and rakyat-friendly dynamic fare mechanism”.
He told a press conference at the Gombak ECRL Terminal that the approval allows fares to be implemented flexibly ahead of the ECRL’s targeted commercial operation in mid-December 2026.
Fares for the 378km Gombak-Kuala Terengganu route will start at RM95 for Transit and RM110 for Express.
The 209km Gombak-KotaSAS route will start at RM60 for Transit and RM68 for Express.
The same starting fares will apply to journeys in the opposite direction.
Transit services will stop at every scheduled station, while Express services will serve only four main stations: Gombak, KotaSAS, Kuala Terengganu and Kota Bharu.
A visitor looks at a screen displaying the ECRL ticket prices at the Gombak Integrated Terminal on October 19, 2026. — Picture by Sayuti Zainudin
Ticket prices may vary according to travel time, demand and seat availability under the dynamic fare mechanism the Cabinet agreed on June 28, 2024, with its implementation formula approved on October 16 this year.
The Express journey from Gombak to Kota Bharu will take about four hours, compared with up to five hours for Transit.
On the Gombak-Kuala Terengganu route, Express will take two hours 54 minutes against three hours 51 minutes for Transit.
The Express trip to KotaSAS will take one hour 27 minutes, compared with two hours five minutes via Transit.
Darwis said children aged two to 12, Malaysian citizens aged 60 and above, cardholders with disabilities and government pensioners will get a 50 per cent discount.
Students aged 13 to 24 will receive a 40 per cent discount, he added.
Asked about ridership, Darwis said MRL is targeting 60 per cent, which it hopes to raise to 90 per cent eventually.
He said no subsidies have been implemented so far and that the project’s success should not be judged on financial returns alone, as the investment is meant to deliver benefits over many years.
Darwis said recouping the RM50.27 billion invested from passenger numbers alone would take “many, many, many years”.
He said revenue would also come from freight operations, and that MRL hopes many companies will use the service to help support operations.
He added that the ECRL’s true success will be measured not by the day the first train departs, but by its ability to save people time, widen economic opportunities and become part of everyday life for generations.
In the initial stage, 10 electric multiple unit (EMU) train sets will run at speeds of up to 160kph, connecting Kelantan, Terengganu, Pahang and Selangor.
The ECRL will run 12 daily trips from Monday to Thursday, with six in each direction.
Services will increase to 16 daily trips from Friday to Sunday, with eight in each direction.
About 2.2 million seats will be made available throughout 2027.
Trains will offer Economy, Premium Economy and Business class, carrying up to 425 passengers in the Economy and Premium Economy configuration and 409 when Business class is included.
Facilities will include luggage racks, a food and beverage counter, a prayer room and dedicated seating for passengers with disabilities.
The trains will also have 4G/5G internet connectivity and Wi-Fi along the route, while LTE-Railway technology will be used for operational communications.
ECRL Operation Sdn Bhd, a joint venture between MRL and China Communications Construction Company Ltd, with each holding a 50 per cent equity interest through their respective joint venture entities, will operate and maintain the railway.
MRL will remain the owner of the ECRL project and its assets.
Darwis said the partnership is meant to ensure safe, efficient and reliable services while building local expertise in Malaysia’s rail industry.
He said the railway is expected to improve connectivity between the East Coast and the Klang Valley, boosting tourism, trade, employment and education and supporting more balanced regional development.
He added that it would also offer an alternative to highway travel, particularly during festive periods and school holidays, when congestion is heaviest.
Official ECRL ticket prices and sales are targeted to be made public in mid-November 2026, while commercial passenger operations on the Gombak-Kota Bharu route are targeted to begin in mid-December.
Darwis said MRL is continuing system testing, safety checks, certification and operational readiness work to ensure a safe and orderly launch.
The public can find more information on fares, schedules and ticket sales on the official ECRL website at
www.ecrl.com.my
, with details for all stations targeted to be published by mid-November.
